correctness.rationale: An exhaustive structural argument classifies all general-position sets from the diameter-two induced-P3 condition; cyclic gap counting proves both polynomials including all boundaries. A decreasing binomial-ratio argument together with explicit positive defect factorizations proves strict log-concavity for every n>=5. Independent exhaustive geodesic verification at n=5..14 and exact-integer checks at n=5..500 corroborate but are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: Complete enumeration and strict log-concavity for a natural, well-defined infinite family address the GP polynomial coefficient-shape problem, while the classification of all inclusion-maximal sets gives a full lower-GP spectrum and a unique six-vertex exception. The structural gap model connects graph geometry to classical cycle independent domination and proves more than a previously known scalar invariant.
